key_insight: A higher polygenic risk score for coronary artery disease was linked to more severe coronary CTA findings, including higher CAD-RADS and CAC.
clinical_relevance: Inherited CAD risk may help explain why some patients present with greater anatomic coronary atherosclerotic burden on routine clinical imaging.
method: 630 Penn Medicine BioBank participants with clinical coronary CTA and genotype data
PRS calculated with a previously published genome-wide score using pgsc_calc
CAD-RADS and CAC were extracted from radiology reports with Llama 3.1 8B and analyzed with Bayesian regression
evidence_signal: LLM-extracted CTA measures matched manual abstraction closely, and each 1-SD increase in PRS was associated with higher CAD-RADS severity (OR 1.20) and higher CAC burden (beta 0.38).
watch_item: This is an observational single-cohort analysis, so clinical adoption would need external validation and careful assessment across ancestry groups and reporting workflows.
paper_title: Association of a polygenic risk score with coronary atherosclerotic burden in clinical CT angiograms
